description: In the NASA Rodent Research-1 (RR-1) validation study, ten 16-week-old female C57BL/6J mice were flown to the ISS for 37 days before euthanasia and subsequent dissection (Flight group). Due to crew time constraint, only two (out of ten) mice were dissected immediately after euthanasia to recover spleen and liver tissues on the ISS. The remaining eight animals were euthanized, then intact carcasses were placed in a pre-chilled cold stowage container and stored in the MELFI. There were respective cohorts of age-matched basal animals which were euthanized one day after launch as a baseline control (Basal control group) as well as age-matched ground control animals kept in an ISS Environmental Simulator at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) on a 4-day delay to mimic spaceflight conditions (Ground control group). In addition, the NASA Validation study also had a cohort of age-matched vivarium control animals that were housed in the vivarium cages and followed the same experimental timeline and process as the spaceflight animals (Vivarium control group). This dataset was generated only from Flight (n of 4) and Ground control (n of 8) animals that were euthanized and preserved intact on-orbit for subsequent dissection on the ground. Libraries were generated using a 3’ Tag-seq approach and sequenced at a depth of 40 M clusters (SE 93 bp).
funding: The sequencing analysis was funded by NASA Space Biology Program Office, Space Life and Physical Sciences Research and Applications Division.

payloads.description:
NASA's Rodent Research Hardware System provides a research platform aboard the International Space Station (ISS) for long-duration rodent experiments in space. Scientists and engineers at Ames Research Center (ARC) developed the new system for the space station based on the Animal Enclosure Module (AEM) that flew aboard 27 space shuttle missions between 1983 and 2011 and supported studies ranging from four to 18 days. Rodent spaceflight experiments have contributed significantly to our understanding of the effects of microgravity on biological processes that are directly relevant to humans in space. 

The maiden voyage of the system, Rodent Research-1 (RR-1), launched on SpaceX-4 CRS-4 on September 21, 2014, and returned October 25, 2014, during ISS expeditions 41/42. Lasting 37 days, RR1 was the longest duration spaceflight rodent study to date conducted in a NASA facility. RR1 was the first mission to transport rodents aboard an unmanned commercial vehicle. The primary goal is for NASA to validate hardware and demonstrate critical research operations, while supporting the Center for the Advancement of Science in Space (CASIS) in sponsoring the first commercial research study.  Ten mice were flown to the ISS and transferred into habitat.  Five mice were wild type (WT) and identified by an ear notch and the remaining mice, called “Knockouts” had no ear notches. Ten mice were used as ground controls.

PI:  Novartis Pharmaceuticals
The mission objectives of the validation flight:

•	The addition of the rodent research system expands the utilization of ISS for research on the effects of microgravity on rodents.
•	The demonstration of the hardware capability to support rodent research for long-duration missions on ISS is accomplished.
•	A validation of the operational capabilities of the hardware to support rodent research provides valuable information applicable to future long-term space missions.
•	Validate that the Rodent Research Hardware can deliver and maintain healthy animals. 
•	Validate that on-orbit activities to support hardware operations can be performed. 
•	Validate that a limited set of generic on-orbit operations can be performed to support future science objectives including but not limited to euthanasia, gross dissection and sample preservation.

Physiological systems of interest for human exploration of space are targeted at the following systems:

•	Bone loss
•	Muscle loss
•	Immune system changes
•	Cardiovascular system changes
•	Nervous system changes.


IACUC Protocol Numbers:  NASA: NAS-13-002-Y1, CASIS: CAS-13-001-Y1

All animal procedures performed in these experiments were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and use Committees (IACUC) numbers NASA: NAS-13-002-Y1 and CASIS: CAS-13-001-Y1 for flight at the NASA Ames Research Center (ARC) and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and the methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations.

The RR-1 payload produced the following Data (from checklist Excel file):

•	Animal enclosure module temperature and relative humidity flight and ground data,
•	Live Animal Return sensor accelerometer data,
•	ISS cabin and ground simulation chamber environmental monitoring data for ppCO2 and RH (AEM-X (Habitat) telemetry data),
•	Rodent data including preflight data, operations time logs, sample shipment data,
•	Daily Health Check Video 
•	Over the Shoulder Camera for all animal operations during Initial Transfer and MSG 
•	Station telemetry data.

Subjects/Biospecimens

RR-1 Basal controls Dissection performed in Colorado 9/12-16/16. BSP tissues collected from the 10 non-treated control group and shipped to ALSDA.

20 Flight: Flight control group Ab Flight experimental group a-M Ab Mice were scanned by a bone densitometer prior to launch and grip strength obtained. During the mission, near the midpoint of inflight operations, live densitometry scans and grip strengths tests were performed. Mice were euthanized at 42 (+ 3 days), hindlimb dissected and whole blood collected. The remaining carcass was frozen at -80C or colder for return. Dissection performed in Colorado 9/12-16/16. BSP tissues collected from the 10 non-treated control group (Ab) and shipped to ALSDA.


NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) Activities
The NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program collected biospecimens from RR-1 to maximize the scientific return from the biological spaceflight.  Rodent Research RR-1 Second Thaw Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) Dissection Summary Report.

Available Data: The RR-1 payload produced the following Data (from checklist Excel file):

-	Animal enclosure temperature and relative humidity flight and ground data
-	Live Animal Return sensor accelerometer data 
-	ISS cabin and ground simulation chamber environmental monitoring data  
-	Rodent data including preflight data, operations time logs, sample shipment data.

protocols.description: A cohort of 16-week-old female C57BL/6J mice were flown to the ISS, housed in the Rodent Habitat and were subjected to microgravity for 37 days. Mice of simiar age, sex and strain were used for ground controls housed in identical hardware and matching ISS environmental conditions. The mice were euthanized by ISS crew with Euthasol injection followed by cervical dislocation, frozen in a pre-chilled Mini Cold Bag (MCB) before transfer to the MELFI freezer (-80 C) and brought back to Earth. The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol was approved by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
protocols.name: Animal Husbandry

protocols.description: The mouse carcasses were removed from -80 C storage and thawed at room temperature for 15-20 minutes. Multiple tissues, were collected from each carcass. Total dissection time for each carcass was no longer than 30 minutes since collection of the first tissue. After harvesting, right gastrocnemius muscle was stored separately overnight at 4 C in RNAlater, then transferred into a -80 C freezer.
protocols.name: Sample Collection

protocols.description: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Germantown, MD) following SOP 3.1-Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNa Mini with Qiagen RNase-Free DNase set. Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Germantown, MD) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 15-20 mg of tissue was weighed and immediately placed in 1.2 mL of the Buffer RLT solution. Tissue homogenization was performed using the Polytron Rotor Stator Homogenizer (Kinematica PT 1300 D) at 15 second intervals for a total of three intervals on an ice bath per the SOP 2.2-Tissue Homogenization using Polytron Rotor Stator Homogenizer. Homogenates were centrifuged for 5 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse-free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following SOP 6.3-QC cDNA. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction

protocols.description: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, Cat 4456739, v92), Mix 1 or Mix 2, were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol. Protocol followed is SOP 5.2 Use of ERCC Spike-In Mixes and UMRR/UHRR Controls for Total RNA Sequencing. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Spike-in Protocol

protocols.description: All samples were normalized to an input of 10ng of total RNA and added to the UPX 3' Transcriptome kit (Qiagen, Germantown, MD), following SOP 5.4-QIAseq UPX 3' Transcriptome Library Preparation. Sample RINs greater than 8.5. Cell IDs, which are used to distinguish individual samples, are added to each sample during the RT step. This allows samples to be pooled together after the RT step and cary out library preparation on a pool of samples as opposed to individual samples. An input of 50ng of pooled cDNA was used to carry out library construction. Library fragment size for this pool of samples is ~540 bp and was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following protocol SOP 6.3-Quality Analysis of Sequencing Libraries Using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Final library concentration and pooled library concentration were measured by qPCR with the QuantSudio 6 Flex Real-Time PCR system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA), following SOP 6.7-Sequencing Library Quantification using QIAseq Library Quant Assay. Library quality control was determined by iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Asymmetric paired end (Read 1: 93bp, Index: 6pb, Read 2: 28bp). PhiX included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.

protocols.description: RThe raw fastq file for each sample was assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.3.2) and raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate raw MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.0.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/tree/NF_RCP_2.0.0/RNAseq/Workflow_Documentation/NF_RCP). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.5) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
